title: Resolving Erdős–Ulam Monochromatic Union-Closed Family Conjectures
description:
We prove both Erdős–Ulam conjectures on monochromatic union-closed families, which are the two specific questions of Erdős Problem 1183. Every two-colouring of the subsets of a finite set contains a monochromatic union-closed family whose size grows faster than any fixed power of the size of the set, while suitable colourings admit no monochromatic union-closed family of exponential size. Both results hold for any number of colours. For families closed under union and intersection, the forced size f(n) satisfies 11n/20 ≤ f(n) ≤ (2+o(1)) n log2 n, so it exceeds the chain bound and is determined up to a logarithmic factor. Counting all union-closed families cannot settle the order of F(n): for n ≥ 206 there are at least 2N−1 of them with N members whenever N ≤ 2n/4. The exact orders of f(n) and F(n), which the problem also asks for, remain open.

This record contains the paper (PDF and LaTeX source with TikZ figures) and the Lean 4 formalisation with Mathlib. Every theorem, proposition and corollary of the paper except Theorem 7.6, and every lemma except Lemmas 7.3, 7.4 and 7.7, is checked in Lean with no sorry. In place of Lemmas 7.3 and 7.4, the formal proof of Lemma 7.1 uses a finite check evaluated by the Lean kernel. The proof of Theorem 7.6 ends in a finite check of 5,308,416 patterns, carried out by four independent programs in C, C++, Python and Julia, which the record contains; Lean carries out the part of it for colourings that depend only on the size of a set. Each audited statement uses only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Claude (Anthropic) assisted with the coding.
